shape_hint: Solid 1:50 tapered pin (nominal d at the SMALL end) with a tapped blind hole (internal metric thread d2, depth t1) in the LARGE end face so a puller screw can extract it; both ends slightly rounded/chamfered (a). Draw as a cone-frustum rod with a threaded counterbored hole at the large end.

role_map.d: nominal diameter at small end of taper, tolerance h10, 1:50 taper
role_map.d2: nominal diameter of internal thread in the large end (coarse pitch)
role_map.a: approximate end crown/rounding dimension (same values as ISO 2339 a)

notes: Internal-thread variant only (ISO 8736 = DIN 7978; Type A ground / B turned). Rows are the ISO 8736 sizes d = 6..20 (6,8,10,12,16,20); larger sizes (25-50) and the DIN-only size 14 are not publishable under T2. Length range per diameter not published (stock-length lists of independent sites differ). IMPORTANT edition conflict: ISO 8736 and DIN 7978 differ in t2 min for d>=20 (28/35/40/40 vs 27/34/42/42) and in 't' at d=40 - hence t2/t omitted. Support counts = independent clusters A,B,C,D,E,F,G that agree on all three columns (C and F might share an origin -> conservative minimum 6). Male-thread ISO 8737 / DIN 7977 data not included (see dropped). INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT: fasteners.eu, boltport.com, ferrofast.com and boltsfastener.com print an identical typo (c max=33 at d=12) on the sibling clevis-pin ISO 2340/DIN 1443 table, so they may share an upstream dataset; their layouts differ so they were counted separately in row_support. Strict count (boltport, boltsfastener/fasenco, fasteners.eu, ferrofast merged into one): rows still have >=4 independent clusters for every kept column (globalfastener/fuller, fasten.it, schrauben-lexikon, that group; plus dm-muehl for d2/a and neue-physik for d2/t1).

B fasten.it: fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_7978 (d1 max, d2 nom 'M4 x 0.7', a, t1 nom, t2 min, t3 nom; DIN 7978 'Withdrawn')

E dm-muehl.de: DIN 7978 page: d1 max/min, d2, 'c ~' -- usable for d2 only (its 'c ~' = a-values but different symbol)

not counted: woodstock7978 (counterbore dia deviates), technifast PDF, huyett/gardette/metalfast/metricmcc (no table)

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched live (HTTP 200): globalfastener ISO 8736, fullerfasteners, fasten.it, boltport, schrauben-lexikon, boltsfastener, fasteners.eu, ferrofast, dm-muehl, neue-physik. Parsed all tables; matrix 6 rows (6,8,10,12,16,20) x 3 columns (d2,a,t1) x 10 pages (gf, fuller, fasten.it, boltport, fasteners.eu, lexikon, boltsfastener, ferrofast, muehl [d2,a], neue-physik [d2,t1]): 0 disagreements (d2 60/60 cells, a 54/54, t1 54/54 incl. t1=18 at d=20). Strict clusters per kept cell: d2 = 6 (A,B,C,D,E,F), t1 = 5 (A,B,C,D,F; E has no t1), a = 4 (A,B,C,D) -> min 4 with explicit-header pages A,B,C(ferrofast),D. Sanity: d2<d, t1=d for d<=16, 18 at d=20, d2 monotone.
problems: Column 'a' dropped for semantics: every page prints only the bare symbol 'a ~' (muehl: 'c ~'); the only textual definition anywhere is fasteners.eu legend 'a - taper' (generic legend that also lists b, which that table does not print; table header there is 'f'), which contradicts the record's 'end rounding/crown' gloss; role was inferred from equality with ISO 2339 'a'. Numbers themselves pass (4 clusters).

fasteners.eu/boltport print 't' and 'f' for t1 and a (and fasteners.eu legend calls 't' 'the depth of the hole'): symbol mapping t->t1, f->a was by value-matching; only ferrofast/boltsfastener (same cluster) and clusters A,B,D carry explicit t1/a headers. Kept t1 because gf/fuller/fasten.it/lexikon/ferrofast all print 't1' and neue-physik words it 'Gewindelaenge' (thread length).
Producer row_support=7 is the lenient count (copy sites counted separately); strict count is 4-6.

Family mismatch: family covers ISO 8736 (internal thread) AND ISO 8737 (external thread) + KS B 1308; record covers ISO 8736/DIN 7978 internal-thread only, d=6..20 of ISO sizes 6..50 (25,30,40,50 and DIN-only 14 not publishable).
t2/t/d1 columns correctly omitted (ISO 8736 vs DIN 7978 edition conflict for d>=20).
Header-order trap on globalfastener: its header table lists d1,P,d2 but data rows run M-thread,P,counterbore-dia; Fuller's labelled rows were used to resolve.
